key_insight: Explainable deep reinforcement learning can optimize residential building energy management while making battery-control decisions more transparent and trustworthy.
engineering_relevance: The framework is relevant for smart buildings with PV and storage because it can reduce electricity costs under dynamic prices, forecasts, and uncertain renewable generation.
method: Trained and compared on-policy and off-policy DRL agents for energy scheduling.
Used an expanded state space with demand, PV output, battery state, weather, prices, forecasts, and calendar/holiday features.
Applied post-hoc explanation methods to interpret the learned policies.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on both synthetic data and real-world Living Lab Energy Campus (LLEC) data, with A2C and PPO showing the best cumulative rewards and policy stability.
watch_item: Performance and interpretability may depend on forecast quality and local building conditions, so policies may need careful validation before deployment.
paper_title: Explainable Data-driven Deep Reinforcement Learning Methods for Optimal Energy Management in Buildings
